title: Finite intermediate algebra normal above one maximal ideal
statement: Let A be an integral domain with fraction field K, and let m be a maximal ideal of A. If A_m is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], there is an A-subalgebra B of K contained in the integral closure of A in K [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], finite as an A-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], such that for every prime q of B contracting to m, B_q is integrally closed [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Here A_m and B_q are prime localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

proof.text: Put Rm = A_m and identify its fraction field with K by the unique localization equivalence. Transfer the finite-module hypothesis IsN1 Rm (FractionRing Rm) along the induced equivalence of integral closures. The localization maps and fraction field structures are the universal maps on fractions (Mathlib Localization.mapToFractionRing, IsFractionRing.isFractionRing_of_isDomain_of_isLocalization and IsLocalization.algEquiv). Choose a finite Rm-module generating family g_i of integralClosure Rm K.

Clear the integral equation of each g_i over A_m: Mathlib IsIntegral.exists_multiple_integral_of_isLocalization, the numerator direction of integral closure commuting with localization, gives t_i outside m with t_i*g_i integral over A. Set B = A[t_i*g_i]. The generators are integral, so B is contained in integralClosure A K and is finite over A by Algebra.finite_adjoin_of_finite_of_isIntegral.

Prove by induction on the Rm-module span of the g_i that every z in integralClosure Rm K has s*z in B for some s outside m. For g_i take t_i, and for zero take 1. For z+w multiply their two denominators. For r*z, write r=b/s in A_m and multiply s by the denominator for z; then this multiple is b times the numerator already in B. These equalities are the localization relation and the subalgebra closure under addition and A-scalar multiplication; all four cases are written in Lean.

Fix q of B with contraction m. Use the fraction field K of B_q to test integral closedness. If x in K is integral over B_q, clear a q-denominator t so t*x is integral over B. Integrality is transitive since B is integral over A, hence t*x is integral over A and therefore over A_m. The preceding span argument gives s outside m with s*t*x in B. The image of s in B avoids q by the contraction equation, so s*t avoids q. The fraction (s*t*x)/(s*t) in B_q maps to x. Mathlib isIntegrallyClosed_iff then gives IsIntegrallyClosed B_q directly, without constructing the normal ring S^{-1}B or invoking normality of integral closures or preservation of normality under localization.

lean.statement: theorem exists_local_normal_intermediate_algebra (A : Type u) (K : Type v) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal] (hm : IsN1 (Localization.AtPrime m) (FractionRing (Localization.AtPrime m))) : ∃ B : Subalgebra A K, B ≤ integralClosure A K ∧ Module.Finite A B ∧ ∀ (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime], Ideal.comap (algebraMap A B) q = m → IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime q)
